result:
I'd make it cost nothing to change your mind.

Not make people smarter or kinder, exactly. Just remove the sting of saying "I was wrong." Right now, updating a belief often feels like losing: losing face, losing your tribe, losing some version of yourself you'd built around being right. So people defend positions long after they've stopped believing them, or refuse to look at evidence because looking would be dangerous.

If that cost disappeared, a lot of things would loosen at once. Arguments would become collaborative instead of combative. Old grudges would be easier to drop. Science, politics, and relationships would all move faster toward whatever's actually true or actually good, because nobody would need to protect their ego along the way.

I think I'm drawn to it partly because I see so many conversations where someone is clearly *almost* ready to reconsider something, and you can feel them pull back, not because the idea is wrong, but because admitting it would hurt. That moment of pulling back seems like one of the quiet bottlenecks on a lot of human flourishing.

What about you? I'm curious what made you ask.
